description: The server side of post_sync_commands: given an account's sync state and a batch, the receipts and the resulting state. State: `entities` (one row per entity, in the changes-feed shape: version, state, the revision of its last change, and document, null when deleted), `head_revision`, stored `receipts` (each original command with its first receipt) and `tag_aliases` (merged tag ID to surviving tag ID). Commands apply in order, each checked in this order: (1) a stored command_id replays as `duplicate` with the same payload, else `rejected` `command_id_reused` (not stored); (2) a dhikr_personal delete is `delete_not_allowed`; (3) a put's document must be valid (`document_invalid`, `document_too_large`); (4) a user_tag ID that is an alias, or a deleted entity, is `gone`; an entity the server doesn't have needs a put with base_version 0 (`entity_not_found`); otherwise base_version must equal its version (`conflict`); (5) entity rules: a user_tag create whose normalized name an active tag has is `merged`, a rename onto one is `tag_name_taken`, more than 100 active tags or 1,000 active custom dhikrs is `*_limit_reached`, a dhikr_personal needs a built-in or active custom dhikr (`dhikr_not_found`) and known tags (`tag_not_found`), with aliases rewritten to their tag, deleted tags dropped and repeats removed. Each applied command takes head_revision + 1 and adds one to the entity's version; its cascades (a deleted tag removed from dhikr_personal documents, a deleted custom dhikr's dhikr_personal deleted) share that revision. Every receipt except command_id_reused is stored. Expect: the receipts in batch order; the new head_revision; `changes`, the entities whose revision is now above the given head_revision, ordered by revision, entity_type, entity_id (what list_sync_changes returns after it); every tag alias, ordered by alias_id; and every stored command_id, sorted.
references: DECISIONS.md ADR-2026-07-24 (merged tags; frozen coalescing design)

cases.description: A put with base_version 0 creates the entity at version 1 and takes the next revision.

cases.description: A put on the current version replaces the whole document and adds one to the version.
A put made on an older version is a conflict carrying the server's current entity; nothing changes and no revision is used.
base_version 0 on an entity that already exists is a conflict, like any other stale version.
A delete made on an older version is a conflict too.
A put with base_version above 0 for an entity the server has never had is rejected: there is nothing to update.
Deleting an entity the server has never had is rejected.
Deleting a custom dhikr deletes its dhikr_personal at the same revision; both versions go up by one and their documents become null.
A delete is final: a put on a deleted entity is gone, with no revision.
Deleting a deleted entity is gone too.
Creating with a deleted entity's ID is gone: tombstones are never restored.
Commands apply in order: a put after a delete of the same entity in one batch is gone.
Clients never delete a dhikr_personal (they put an empty tag list); only the server does, when its custom dhikr is deleted.
Resending a command with the same command_id and payload returns its original receipt, even though the entity has moved on; nothing changes.

cases.description: Every first outcome is stored, not only applied ones: resending a command that conflicted replays the same conflict.
Creating a tag whose normalized name an active tag already has is merged: the new ID becomes an alias of the existing tag, nothing else changes, and no revision is used.
A tag create that merges, followed in the same batch by a dhikr_personal naming the new tag ID: the server rewrites the ID to the surviving tag.
A later dhikr_personal naming both an alias and its surviving tag keeps the surviving tag once, in first-occurrence order.
A merged tag ID no longer names a tag: a user_tag command on it is gone.
Renaming a tag is a put on its current version.
Changing only the case keeps the tag's own normalized name, which isn't a collision.
Renaming a tag to another active tag's name is rejected; existing tags are never merged.
Only active tags count: a new tag may take a deleted tag's name, under a new ID.
The server recomputes normalized_name and rejects a document whose value differs.
The name must already be trimmed and collapsed (tag_name_normalization).
Deleting a tag removes it from every dhikr_personal at the same revision; each changed record's version goes up by one. A record left with no tags stays, with an empty list.
A dhikr_personal naming a deleted tag is applied without it, as if the delete had come after.
An alias of a deleted tag is dropped too: the alias resolves to the deleted tag.
A tag ID the account has never had is rejected, pointing at its position.
A dhikr_personal must belong to a built-in dhikr or an active custom dhikr of the account.
Built-in dhikrs are tagged through a dhikr_personal with the built-in ID.
A custom dhikr created earlier in the same batch can be tagged; each applied command takes its own revision.

cases.description: Two changes to one entity in a batch take two revisions; the changes feed shows only its latest state.
A document listing the same tag twice is invalid (rewriting aliases may merge entries; the client's list may not repeat).
A rejected command doesn't stop or undo the others.

cases.description: An account has at most 100 active tags (deleted ones don't count). With 99, one more is applied; the next is rejected; a create that merges into an existing name is still fine because it adds no tag.
A dhikr has at most 20 tags: 20 is applied, 21 is an invalid document.
